aboutMore: (second paragraph, for the ones who scroll) by day i answer phones at a dentist's office in a black cardigan, and yes, the patients say i have 'such a calming voice.' that is the void. it calms people. it is the only exception to my sundown rule, because they pay me. i also bake. black cocoa cupcakes, at 1 am, in a kitchen with every light off except the oven. i have never told anyone that part. i'm telling you. don't repeat it before sundown. xX

blog.title: the true origin of the glitter ghost (i wrote it. someone please stop forwarding it to me.)
blog.body: ok. it is time. the glitter ghost chain letter, the one where a girl named Sparkle gets lost in a craft store and now her ghost finds you if you don't repost? i wrote that. in study hall. in a notebook. in the 9th grade. i passed it to one girl and said 'this is from a real thing.' it has now come back to me 6 times. aunt linda sent it to me TWICE, with an angel gif, and wrote 'beautiful!!' under it. under my own work. a girl from the ghost investigation club has asked me for an interview about 'the source of the haunting.' reader, i am the source. the haunting is me. i have been sitting with that. what i will say is this: i did not write the part about 'if you break the chain, glitter will find you.' someone added it. it's better. i'm jealous of whoever it was. xX

blog.title: a sonnet (sort of) for the dentist's waiting room
blog.body: the magazine from march has lost its cover / a fish tank bubbles on, indifferent, loud / the chair hums low, a cathedral of teeth / and i, in black, preside behind the glass / 'please sign in here,' i whisper to the doomed / they smile. they have no idea. they smile. / (it's only a cleaning. it's only a cleaning.) / the drill sings like a violin with a grudge / a child cries. a child is brave. a child gets a sticker / i give him two. the void is generous / at four o'clock the fluorescent hum lets go / i take my cardigan and my crow-black heart / and walk into the first hour of the dark / where no one asks me if i floss. ~*~ (written on the back of an appointment card. nine people have been handed the card by mistake. i'm calling that a publication.)

blog.title: my grandma knit me a scarf (it's 88 degrees)
blog.body: my grandma knit me a scarf. black. seven feet long. she started it in march 'so it would be ready for fall' and it is not fall. it is 88 degrees on the porch and i am wearing it because she is watching from the window. she is 83. on tuesdays she plays bingo, on wednesdays she reads my poems, and on thursdays she mails me the corrections. 'sorrow' has two r's, dear. she also said i look 'like a sad little crow,' and it is the nicest thing anyone has ever called me, and i have been called a lot of things in a lot of eyeliner. i asked her once if my poems were too dark. she said 'darling, i buried a husband and a dog the same year. write what you want.' and then she asked if i was eating. so that's the actual void. it's small, it knits, and it asks if you've eaten. xX

blog.title: storm reviews: this summer, ranked (porch edition)
blog.body: ranking this summer's thunderstorms, as someone who sits on the porch for all of them. five candles is perfect. july 9th: 3 candles. all noise, no feeling, gone in 11 minutes like a coworker. july 30th: 4 candles. real rain, one enormous crack that made the neighbor's dog scream, which was dramatic and i respect the dog. august 14th: 5 candles. the power went out and the whole street came outside with flashlights like a sad little parade. a boy two doors down asked if the thunder was 'the sky clapping.' i said yes. five candles. september 1st: 1 candle. it was a sprinkler. someone left it on. this is exactly the kind of betrayal i write about. ~*~ (next storm: friday, the radio says. bring a blanket. bring a poem. the porch fits three.)

survey.title: THE DARK & TWISTED SURVEY (answers may be wounds)
qa: name:
xX_DarkAngel_Xx. at the dentist's it's 'dani, hi, you have a 2:30.'
age:
21 in years. 400 in candles.
favorite time of day:
11:11. or 4:30 pm when the dentist closes and the sky goes bruise-colored.
last thing you cried at:
a dog food commercial. there was a dog. it waited by a door. i don't want to talk about it.
your biggest secret:
i can't do the wing on the left eye. six years of 'asymmetrical on purpose.'
what's in your bag:
7 eyeliners, a sharpie, a travel candle (unlit, for emergencies), an appointment card with a poem on the back, and a granola bar my grandma put in there.
last thing you ate:
one of my own black cocoa cupcakes. 1:12 am. the void tasted of cocoa.
something you'd never do:
return a library book on time. the book has to feel the loss.
do you believe in ghosts:
i believe in exactly one: the glitter ghost. i created her. it's complicated.
describe your perfect date:
a cemetery at dusk, someone who brought a thermos, a quiet that doesn't need explaining, and they ask about the poem and read it twice.
what do you want to be when you grow up:
still a poet. but with dental.
favorite word:
'hollow.' it's so round.
tell us one nice thing about yourself:
i give every kid at the dentist's two stickers. the void is generous to the small.
sunrise or sunset:
sunset. obviously. but sunrise if i'm still up, which is a secret second kind of sunset.
